findings.summary: The numbered section headings do not run in sequence and repeat, so a learner cannot follow the part's structure.
findings.evidence: Heading order across the four pages is: "2. Toolkit For Empty Images", "3. Mounts Aren't Showing", "2. Security Posture" | "4. Reproduce It Minimally", "5. What Each Layer Costs", "1. Storage Speed Truth", "4. The Model, One Line" | "3. The Operational Trade", "4. Volume Drivers", "5. Six Lines To Keep" | "6. Back Up A Volume", "7. DNS In One Box", "8. Prune Safely" — i.e. 2,3,2,4,5,1,4,3,4,5,6,7,8, with no section 1 on the opening page and "2" and "4" each used twice.
findings.fix: Renumber every heading in a single ascending run across the part (1..N), and give page 1's opening bullets/table/MTU Q&A an explicit "1." heading so the sequence starts at 1.

findings.summary: The caption's first sentence is a flat series label rather than a hook, burying the actual hook in sentence two.
findings.evidence: "Part 2 of DOCKER NETWORKING & VOLUMES. Your container can't be reached and your database just vanished — same root cause: ..."
findings.fix: Lead with the hook and move the part label later or to the end: "Your container can't be reached and your database just vanished — same root cause: namespaces gave it a private network and a disposable filesystem. (Part 2 of DOCKER NETWORKING & VOLUMES.) This handbook walks the whole path: ..."

findings.summary: The symptom table maps "refused between containers" to "not on the same network", which contradicts the page's own rule that a refusal proves the packet arrived.
findings.evidence: Bullet: "A refusal proves the packet arrived; a timeout does not." Table row: ["refused between containers","not on the same network"]. Docker isolates bridge networks with a DROP rule (DOCKER-ISOLATION-STAGE-1/2, now DOCKER-FORWARD/DOCKER-BRIDGE), not a REJECT, so cross-network traffic hangs and times out; by name it fails DNS resolution instead.
findings.fix: Change the row to "refused between containers" → "target service bound to 127.0.0.1, or wrong port", and move "not on the same network" to the timeout row (or to the existing "name not found" row).

findings.summary: The mandated first debugging step is introduced after the MTU deep-dive and the netshoot toolkit, and is filed under the toolkit heading.
findings.evidence: "Step 1 always: `docker inspect c` — `.NetworkSettings`, `.Mounts`." appears as the sixth block on the page, below the symptom table, the "Ping is fine but uploads hang?" MTU Q&A, the heading "2. Toolkit For Empty Images" and the netshoot code block.
findings.fix: Move the bullets block containing `docker inspect`, `docker port`, `ss -ltnp` and `tcpdump -i docker0` to the top of page 1 under its own "1. Start With inspect" heading, and leave the symptom table, MTU Q&A and netshoot toolkit after it.

findings.summary: Security-posture material opens on the debugging page, before the trade-offs material it belongs to, and is then split into three disconnected fragments.
findings.evidence: Page 1 ends with heading "2. Security Posture" and "-p 127.0.0.1:5432:5432   # narrow, or none"; page 2 ends with "Databases on `--internal` nets with no published ports." and "Secrets: tmpfs or a manager"; page 3 then opens with the "inspect Leaks" callout and "Why never mount docker.sock?" — with the performance bullets, the write-path table and the model diagram wedged between them.
findings.fix: Delete the "2. Security Posture" heading and code block from page 1 and merge it with the page 2 security bullets and the page 3 docker.sock/inspect blocks into one contiguous security section placed after the performance/cost material.

findings.summary: The claim that only userns-remap breaks the docker.sock-equals-host-root equivalence is wrong: remapping does not contain socket access, and rootless Docker is omitted.
findings.evidence: "Daemon access is ==root on the host==, full stop." / "Only `userns-remap` breaks that equivalence." An attacker holding the socket can simply request `--userns=host` (which Docker also requires for `--privileged`), opting that container out of the daemon-wide remapping and regaining real host root.
findings.fix: Replace with: "userns-remap does not contain socket access — the API lets a caller request `--userns=host`. Only rootless Docker (unprivileged daemon) or a filtering socket proxy changes the equation."

findings.summary: The closing cheat sheet starts on page 3 but three new instructional sections follow on page 4, so the summary is interrupted by fresh teaching.
findings.evidence: Page 3 ends with "5. Six Lines To Keep" plus the mount-defaults table and the volume-seeding bullets, after which page 4 introduces new material: "6. Back Up A Volume" with the `tar czf /backup/v.tgz` idiom, "7. DNS In One Box", and "8. Prune Safely".
findings.fix: Reorder so the backup, DNS and prune sections come before "Six Lines To Keep", leaving the cheat sheet, the debug-order callout and the "Final Model" callout as the last blocks of the part.

findings.summary: A pushpin sticker is drawn on top of the tar command's `-C` flag, obscuring the flag characters in a copyable command.
findings.evidence: Code block in "6. Back Up A Volume": `tar czf /backup/v.tgz -C /data .` — the pin graphic sits directly over the `-C` token, and the sticky note "restore by untarring into a fresh volume" is anchored beneath it.
findings.fix: Move the pin/sticky-note anchor to the right margin of the code block (after `/data .`) or below the final code line so no glyphs are covered.

findings.summary: A pushpin sticker overlaps the resolver IP inside the DNS code block, hiding part of `127.0.0.11`.
findings.evidence: Code block under "7. DNS In One Box": `# expect nameserver 127.0.0.11` — the pin graphic covers the characters between `127.0` and `0.11`, with the note "Alpine musl DNS can be flaky" attached below.
findings.fix: Anchor that sticky note to the empty space to the right of the code block instead of on the comment line, so the IP renders unobstructed.

findings.summary: `tcpdump -i docker0` captures only the legacy default bridge, which the part elsewhere tells readers never to use.
findings.evidence: "`tcpdump -i docker0` watches the bridge itself." versus page 3: "Always a user-defined bridge: free DNS and real isolation." A user-defined network's host interface is `br-<net-id>` (see `docker network inspect -f '{{.Id}}'`), so this command shows nothing for the recommended setup.
findings.fix: Write it as `tcpdump -i br-<net-id>` (docker0 only for the default bridge), e.g. `tcpdump -i br-$(docker network inspect -f '{{.Id}}' n | cut -c1-12)`.

findings.summary: A list of networking mistakes is placed under the storage-performance heading, where none of its items apply.
findings.evidence: Under heading "1. Storage Speed Truth" (and after the write-path table) the cross-style bullets read: "Publishing on 0.0.0.0 out of habit.", "Hardcoding container IPs — they move on restart.", "Trusting **UFW**: Docker writes its own iptables rules.", "`--link` instead of a user-defined network."
findings.fix: Move that cross-style bullets block out of the storage section — place it with the networking/security section — or give it its own heading such as "Networking Anti-Patterns".

findings.summary: The driver table credits the bridge driver with "DNS by name" unqualified, contradicting the part's own (correct) statements that the default bridge has no name resolution.
findings.evidence: Table row: ["bridge","default, NAT, DNS by name"], versus page 1 "name not found → default bridge — no DNS" and page 4 "Per-network — the default bridge resolves **nothing**."
findings.fix: Qualify the cell: "default, NAT, DNS by name on user-defined nets only".

findings.summary: A pushpin sticker overlaps the end of the `--opt device=` line in the volume-create code block.
findings.evidence: Code block under "4. Volume Drivers": `--opt device=:/exports/data` — the pin graphic lands on the final characters of `/exports/data`, with the note "NFS through the local driver" below it.
findings.fix: Offset the pin/note anchor to the right of the code block's text column so the path string is fully visible.

findings.summary: The volume-driver section claims the NFS mount goes through the local driver, but the example command never shows the driver being selected.
findings.evidence: Code block: "docker volume create nfsvol \\  --opt type=nfs \\  --opt o=addr=10.0.0.5,rw \\  --opt device=:/exports/data" with note "NFS through the local driver".
findings.fix: Add `--driver local` to the example so the note's claim is visible in the command.

findings.summary: The volume-deletion table is separated from the prune-safety warnings by the backup and DNS sections.
findings.evidence: Page 4's first block is the table with rows "docker rm -v | anonymous volumes only", "compose down -v | project volumes", "volume prune | unused anonymous volumes..."; the matching warnings ("Pruning blind — list `docker volume ls -f dangling=true` first.", "Running `compose down -v` on a stack holding real data.") appear seven blocks later under "8. Prune Safely".
findings.fix: Place the "8. Prune Safely" heading and its cross-style bullets immediately after the deletion table, and move the backup and DNS sections below them.
